requirements.title: Minimum 20 Percent Non-Federal Cost Share
requirements.description: WCPP requires a non-Federal cost share of 20 percent from all recipients unless an exception applies; applicants who do not provide the required match will be classified as ineligible.
appliesWhen: Unless an exception applies, such as 100 percent federal share for certain safety projects or sliding scale adjustments

Budget showing match funds

requirements.title: Previously Incurred Costs Not Counted Toward Match

requirements.title: State Highway Agency Consultation Documentation Required
requirements.description: If an application is submitted by an eligible entity other than a State DOT or FLMA, the application must include documentation that the State highway agency (or equivalent) was consulted during development of the application; failure to provide sufficient documentation makes the application ineligible.
appliesWhen: Applicant is not a State DOT or FLMA
For Tribes, only required for projects not located on Tribal lands
evidenceNeeded: Documentation of consultation with State highway agency or equivalent

sources.quote: If an application is submitted by an eligible entity other than a State DOT or an FLMA, the application shall include documentation that the State highway agency, or an equivalent of that agency, of the State in which the eligible entity is located, was consulted during the development of the application (23 U.S.C. 171(d)(2)). For Tribes, such consultation shall be required only for projects not located on Tribal lands. DOT will not review applications that fail to provide sufficient documentation of consultation, and such applications will not be eligible for funding.

requirements.title: State DOT Administration Requirement for Non-FLMA/Tribe Recipients
requirements.description: If the grant recipient is any eligible entity other than an Indian Tribe or an FLMA, the State DOT of the State in which the project is located must administer the grant, either directly or as a pass-through entity; these recipients may not request FHWA to administer the grant directly, and FHWA cannot award if the State DOT does not agree.
appliesWhen: Grant recipient is not an Indian Tribe or FLMA
evidenceNeeded: Documentation or agreement showing State DOT will administer or oversee the grant

sources.quote: If the grant recipient is any eligible entity other than an Indian Tribe or an FLMA, then, pursuant to 23 U.S.C. 171(f)(2)(A)(ii), the State DOT of the State in which the project is located must administer the grant. For these recipients, the State DOT must directly administer the project on behalf of the recipient or administer and oversee the project by serving as a pass-through entity for the recipient (23 U.S.C. 171(f)(2)(A)(ii)). These recipients may not request FHWA to administer the grant directly. FHWA cannot award a grant to these recipients if the State DOT does not agree to administer the grant.
